info.title: Simple Host API
info.description: Static website hosting with a light per-site backend. Deploy a site with one API call — inline JSON files (LLM-friendly) or a tar.gz/zip archive — and each site gets shared JSON state (with atomic ops) and saved data of four kinds (Page info, Submissions, Personal, Shared board) on top of per-site lists. Sign-in is a 6-digit email code or Google that returns an API key, sent as the `X-API-Key` header. Hosted-page sign-in uses the same account but a site-scoped session cookie on the site's own address — never an API key. Every site lives at its own address, `https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.site/` (its own browser origin); `https://<handle>.simple-host.site/` lists the person's public sites. For a brand-new account a site may briefly live at `https://<handle>.simple-host.site/<site>/` until its certificate is issued: use the `site_url` the API returns, never a composed one. Old `<handle>.simple-host.app/<site>/` links redirect to the site's address, as do old `sites.simple-host.app/<handle>/<site>/` ones. Visitors sign in with Google or an emailed code on the site's own address (a sign-in covers that site only); every save from a page needs a signed-in visitor. Agents save with the API key (or the connector) through `https://simple-host.app/v1/...`.

servers.description: Production API (agents, with an API key). Pages call the same /v1 routes same-origin on their own address.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Email-code sign-in and dashboard OAuth handoff (`/?token=`)

tags.name: Visitor
tags.description: Site-scoped browser session for hosted-page Google or email-code sign-in, on the site's own address (its address `https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.site/`, or its domain if it has one). Same `users` row as email-code / dashboard OAuth; the cookie is not an API key and does not satisfy owner routes.

tags.name: Deploy
tags.description: Create/update a site (JSON files or archive)

tags.name: State
tags.description: Per-site shared JSON store (reads public — a request from a page is Origin-checked, one with no Origin/Referer is served; writes from a page need a signed-in visitor on the site's own address, agents write with the site owner's key; another account's key gets 404). A site with a connected domain lives there — its `https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.site/...` address answers 302 to `https://<domain>/...` (same path and query) and writes through that address answer 401 use_custom_domain; agents write through the apex.

tags.description: Per-site lists (POST is a write; declared kinds under /data)

tags.name: Custom domains
tags.description: Give a site a nicer address — a free <name>.simple-host.site or one custom domain (CNAME or A record plus a TXT ownership record; its certificate is issued automatically once both are seen). Optional.

get.summary: Skills hub catalog — discover the bundled agent skills
get.description: Public catalog of the skills this server bundles (name + description + fetch URL), so any agent can search them over HTTP. No auth.

get.summary: Fetch one skill's SKILL.md (markdown)
get.description: Returns the raw SKILL.md for the named skill. Public, no auth.

404.description: No such skill

get.summary: Fetch one skill's SKILL.md (markdown), same as /v1/skills/{name}
get.description: Same response as /v1/skills/{name}. Public, no auth.

404.description: No such skill

get.summary: Fetch one of a skill's reference documents (markdown)
get.description: A skill's SKILL.md routes to reference documents under its references/ directory. A folder install has them on disk; install methods that fetch only SKILL.md by URL do not, so SKILL.md cites each reference by absolute URL as well and this endpoint serves it. Public, no auth.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The reference filename, e.g. backend.md

400.description: Invalid skill or reference name

404.description: No such reference

post.summary: Request a sign-in code
post.description: Emails a 6-digit code (and a magic link) to the address. No user row is created here — the account is created lazily on the first successful verify, so this can't be used to enumerate users.

nonce_hash.description: Browser pages only. base64url SHA-256 of a random nonce the page keeps. With it the email also carries a sign-in link, redeemable only together with that nonce (so only in that browser). Without it the email carries the code alone.

post.summary: Verify the code and get an API key
post.description: Exchange `{email, code}` (CLI/agent) or a magic-link `{token}` (browser) for an API key. The first successful email-code verify creates the account. Dashboard Google also redeems through this endpoint (`/?token=&cn=`). A link token is redeemed only with the `nonce` whose hash it was issued with, so a sign-in link works only in the browser that asked for it. Visitor-issued codes are not accepted here. The code expires in 15 minutes and allows 3 attempts.

nonce.description: required with token — the nonce whose hash was sent when the link was requested

name.description: Optional label for the key this sign-in issues, shown in the Keys list (GET /v1/me/keys). Defaults to "dashboard sign-in" for a link or Google, "agent sign-in" for a typed code.

choose_handle.description: When this sign-in would create a new account: create nothing yet and answer 409 with code choose_handle and a suggested_handle, without using up the code. Ask the person which address they want, then verify again with the same code and handle. Ignored for an existing account.

handle.description: The address (<handle>.simple-host.site) a NEW account takes; ignored for an existing account. Refused as 400 invalid_handle, 409 handle_reserved or 409 handle_taken without using up the code, so another can be tried. It can be changed later (PATCH /v1/me), not more than once in 30 days after publishing. Without handle or choose_handle a new account is given one.

409.description: code choose_handle (a new account: choose its address first; carries suggested_handle and address), or handle_taken / handle_reserved (the handle sent cannot be had; error names the address). The code is not used up.

401.description: Invalid or expired code

get.summary: Is this address (handle) free?
get.description: Whether <handle>.simple-host.site can be taken as an account's address: at sign-up (POST /v1/auth/verify with handle) or as a change (PATCH /v1/me). Handles, old handles that still redirect, free <name>.simple-host.site addresses claimed by sites, other accounts' live site names (an unclaimed <name>.simple-host.site still redirects to that site) and reserved names share one namespace. With X-API-Key the account's own handle counts as available. Rate limited per address (RATE_LIMIT_HANDLE_CHECK); no CORS, and a cross-site browser request gets 403. A claim still decides.

error.example: That address is taken: rose.simple-host.site is already in use. Try another.

429.description: Too many checks from this address

get.summary: List enabled OAuth providers
get.description: Google (more providers later). Public discovery for pages and the dashboard. Returns the enabled provider names (`google`) so pages never hardcode a provider. Empty when sign-in is not configured. Sign-in creates or links a `users` row; a hosted-page session still does not disclose an API key.

email_enabled.description: Whether email sign-in codes are configured

get.summary: Start OAuth
get.description: Apex start. Query `return_to` is required and must be an absolute URL. Two shapes: the dashboard origin `/` (owner purpose — callback hands off via `/?token=`; success 302s to the provider with PKCE S256) or a site's own address — a site host `https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.site/...` (or, while that person's certificate is pending, the person address `https://<handle>.simple-host.site/<site>/...`), a claimed name or a DNS-proven bound domain (site purpose). A site-purpose start is not begun here: it 302s to `GET /v1/visitor/oauth/{provider}` on that site's own host, which binds the sign-in to the browser. Unknown or disabled provider is 404. No cookie is set here. The Legacy path-address (`sites.<domain>/<handle>/<site>/`) return_to URLs are rejected with 400 invalid return_to, as are apex URLs outside the dashboard. The caller cannot set `purpose`; it is derived from `return_to`.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: Absolute URL of the page to return to after sign-in

400.description: Invalid or missing return_to

404.description: Unknown or disabled provider

get.summary: OAuth callback
get.description: Provider redirect URI on the apex. Consumes the one-time `state`. Identifies via userinfo, then `resolveUser` (link or create a `users` row on a verified email; refuse missing/unverified email). Site purpose 302s to `https://<return-host>/v1/visitor/establish?once=…`. Owner purpose 302s to `{PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/?token=…` for the dashboard to redeem via `POST /v1/auth/verify`. Neither redirect contains an API key. Failures are a short no-store HTML page on the apex with no Location and no cookie.

302.description: Site purpose: redirect to /v1/visitor/establish on the stored host. Owner purpose: redirect to /?token= on PUBLIC_BASE_URL.

400.description: Bad, replayed, or expired state, or provider error

404.description: Unknown or disabled provider

get.summary: Start visitor sign-in on the site's own host
get.description: Visitor sign-in start, served on the site's own address (its `<site>.<handle>` host, person address, claimed name or bound domain). `return_to` must be a page on this same host that belongs to the site served here. Sets a short-lived host-only nonce cookie (`__Host-sh_vnonce`, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, 10 minutes; `sh_vnonce` on local HTTP), stores only its SHA-256 with the OAuth state, and 302s to the provider with PKCE S256. `GET /v1/visitor/establish` later sets the session only in the browser holding that nonce, so a sign-in finished elsewhere cannot be completed in another browser (login CSRF). auth.js `SH.signIn()` navigates here.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: Absolute URL of a page on this host to return to after sign-in

302.description: Nonce cookie set; redirect to the identity provider

400.description: Missing return_to, or one that is not a page of the site on this host

404.description: Unknown or disabled provider

get.summary: Establish the visitor session cookie
get.description: One-time hop on the site's own address (its `<site>.<handle>` host or domain). Consumes `once`, host-matches, requires the `__Host-sh_vnonce` cookie set by `GET /v1/visitor/oauth/{provider}` in this browser (its hash must match the one bound to the code; the code is burned on any failure), sets `__Host-sh_vsess` (or `sh_vsess` on local HTTP), clears the nonce cookie, then 302s to the stored `return_to` with no query mutation. Never sets a cookie on the apex or the legacy path address. Failures are HTML, no cookie, no redirect.

302.description: Cookie set; redirect to the stored return_to

400.description: Bad, replayed, expired, host-mismatch, missing or wrong nonce cookie, or apex Host

post.summary: Log out this visitor session
post.description: Deletes the session named by the visitor cookie and clears the cookie. Requires `X-SH-CSRF: 1` or `Content-Type: application/json` (not a simple form post).

403.description: Missing CSRF header (and not a JSON request)

patch.summary: Edit display name or change your handle
patch.description: Changing the handle changes every address (https://<handle>.simple-host.site/ and https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.site/). Before anything is published it changes freely. After that (even once every site is gone) it can change once every 30 days: the old handle stays reserved for this account and every old address redirects to the new one. A new handle gets its own certificate; until it is issued, sites briefly use the fallback https://<handle>.simple-host.site/<site>/. What pages kept in visitors' browsers starts empty at the new address, and visitors sign in again.

display_name.description: Trimmed; empty clears the name. Never used in URLs.

handle.description: The <handle> in your address https://<handle>.simple-host.site/. Must not be reserved or already taken (handles and free <name>.simple-host.site addresses share one namespace).

signin_alerts.description: Sign-in alert emails (default true): one email after each sign-in or app connection, at most one per browser or app a day. Needs one of the account's own API keys (a connected app or the admin key gets 400 not_an_account_key).

400.description: Invalid profile, or signin_alerts sent without an account key (code not_an_account_key)

401.description: API key required

409.description: The handle cannot be had: code handle_taken (another account's handle or old handle, or a site's claimed free name; error says "That address is taken: <handle>.simple-host.site is already in use. Try another.") or handle_reserved. A malformed handle is 400 invalid_handle.

429.description: The handle already changed within the last 30 days after publishing

get.summary: Current user

handle.description: The <handle> in your addresses: sites at https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.site/, your page at https://<handle>.simple-host.site/

public_page.description: The account's public page listing its public sites, e.g. https://<handle>.simple-host.site/. Present with handle.

signin_alerts.description: Whether an email follows each sign-in or app connection (PATCH /v1/me to change).

delete.summary: Delete your account and all its data
delete.description: Deletes the account at once and for good; nothing goes to Recently deleted and nothing can be restored. Removed: every site (including ones in Recently deleted) with its files, versions, saved data, lists and analytics; keys; connected apps; visitor sign-ins; and every entry this person sent to other people's lists while signed in; their address is taken off the changes they made to other people's page data (writes made without signing in and older public-list entries are not linked to anyone and stay; support@simple-host.app helps with those). The handle, old handles and claimed <name>.simple-host.site addresses are retired, never given to anyone else; custom domains are released. A confirmation email goes to the account's address. Offer GET /v1/me/export.zip first. Refused for a suspended account or one holding a site the operator took down (the operator handles those), an admin account, or one still holding event hostnames.

confirm.description: The account's handle, or its email when it has no handle. Case-insensitive.

400.description: confirm missing (code confirm_required) or does not match (code confirm_mismatch)

403.description: Suspended account (code account_suspended), a site of the account taken down (code site_suspended) or admin account (code admin_account)

409.description: The account still holds event hostnames (code event_hostnames)

429.description: Too many requests from this address

post.summary: Change your sign-in email, step 1: send codes to the new and the current address
post.description: Emails a 6-digit code to the new address and another to the current one (15 minutes, 3 tries). Send both to POST /v1/me/email/verify to finish. Asking looks the same for every address. Needs one of the account's own API keys: a connected app or the admin key gets 400 not_an_account_key. Refused for the plugin reviewer account (and for moving any account to its address), admin, event and preview accounts, and accounts whose sign-in name is not an email address. Rate-limited per address and per account, like sign-in.

400.description: Not an account key (code not_an_account_key), not an email (code invalid_email), already the sign-in email (code same_email), or the reviewer's address (code reserved_email)

403.description: The reviewer, an admin, event or preview account, or one with no email to confirm from (codes reviewer_account, admin_account, event_account, preview_account, no_current_email)

post.summary: Change your sign-in email, step 2: confirm with both codes
post.description: Moves the account to the new address: from now on sign-in codes go there. The handle, sites and connected apps stay; every other API key of the account is signed out (the one making the call stays); linked Google/GitHub sign-ins stay (GET /v1/me/identities lists them). Open sign-in codes for the old address stop working, the account's emailed idle-site links end, and the old address gets a notice naming the new one masked (n***@example.com) with an undo link valid for 7 days. An address another account signs in with is refused here, after the codes are verified (409 email_taken). Needs one of the account's own API keys.

code.description: The 6-digit code emailed to the new address

current_code.description: The 6-digit code emailed to the current address

400.description: Not an account key (code not_an_account_key), a code missing (code codes_required), no change waiting (code no_pending_change), or the reviewer's address (code reserved_email)

401.description: Wrong or expired code, or too many tries (code invalid_code)

403.description: The reviewer, an admin, event or preview account (see step 1)

409.description: Another account signs in with that address (code email_taken)

get.summary: "This wasn't me" link from the old address's notice (confirmation page)
get.description: Shows a page with an Undo button and changes nothing. No sign-in; the token is the authorization. 404 page when the link was used or is older than 7 days. Emailed links carry the token in the fragment (`#t=`), so it never reaches a server log: without `t` the GET returns a small page whose script posts the fragment's token back with `peek=1`, which shows this confirmation. Links sent before v0.7.1 carry `?t=` and keep working until they expire.

200.description: HTML confirmation page with the button

404.description: HTML page; the link was used or has expired

post.summary: Undo a sign-in email change
post.description: The confirmation page's button (with `peek=1`, only the confirmation page). Puts the account back on the old address, signs out every API key and every sign-in on sites, removes Google/GitHub sign-ins and connected apps added since the change, and spends every undo link of the account. HTML page.

200.description: HTML page; the account signs in with the old address again

404.description: HTML page; the link was used or has expired

409.description: HTML page; another account signs in with the old address now

get.summary: Google and GitHub accounts that sign in to yours
get.description: Own API key only (400 not_an_account_key otherwise).

400.description: Not an account key (code not_an_account_key)

delete.summary: Unlink a Google or GitHub sign-in
delete.description: That Google or GitHub account no longer signs in to yours. Own API key only.

400.description: Not an account key (code not_an_account_key)

404.description: No such sign-in on this account

get.summary: Download all your data (one .zip)
get.description: Streams one .zip of everything held about the account: README.txt; account.json (email, handle, display name, created, earlier handles, claimed names including retired ones, custom domains, linked Google/GitHub sign-ins); keys.json (name, last 4 characters, created, last used; never keys or hashes); connected_apps.json (name, connected, last used); visitor.json (sites signed in to as a visitor with first sign-in and last seen, every entry sent to other people's lists while signed in, and `changed`: every change made to other people's page data or list entries while signed in, as site, what, change and when); sites/<name>/ for every live site in the same layout as GET /v1/sites/{sitename}/export.tar.gz (files/, state.json, collections.json); and recently-deleted/<name>/ for every site in Recently deleted, in the same layout plus deleted.json (deleted_at, removed_for_good_at). Visitor analytics hold no personal data (salted hashes) and are not included. Needs one of the account's own API keys: a connected app or the admin key gets 400 not_an_account_key. A suspended account gets 403 account_suspended and writes to support@simple-host.app for a copy of its data.

400.description: Not one of the account's own API keys (code not_an_account_key)

403.description: The account is suspended (code account_suspended); write to support@simple-host.app for a copy of the data

get.summary: Download all your data (older address)
get.description: The address Download my data had before it became a .zip. Serves exactly what GET /v1/me/export.zip serves: the same .zip, with Content-Type application/zip and a .zip filename, under the same rules. Use /v1/me/export.zip.

400.description: Not one of the account's own API keys (code not_an_account_key)

post.summary: Sign out everywhere (rotate your API key)
post.description: The "Sign out everywhere" button. Replaces all of the authenticated owner's API keys with one new key and returns it. Every older key stops working immediately, and every connected app (see /v1/me/connections) is disconnected. Keys are stored only as SHA-256 hashes, so this response is the only time the new key is shown.

get.summary: List connected apps
get.description: The AI apps (ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, a GPT Action) this account has connected through the Simple Host connector (OAuth at /oauth/authorize, MCP at /mcp). Each is listed once, however many times it was connected.

name.description: The name the app registered with

device.description: The browser the connection was approved on, summarised, to tell two connections of the same app apart. Never the user agent itself or an IP. Empty when unknown (and for connections made before 2026-09-27).

get.summary: List recently deleted sites
get.description: Sites this account deleted in the last 7 days. Each keeps its files, versions, saved data, collections and addresses, and its name stays taken, until purge_at; POST /v1/sites/{sitename}/restore brings it back until then.

200.description: Recently deleted sites, most recently deleted first

purge_at.description: When it is removed for good

delete.summary: Disconnect an app
delete.description: Revokes every token this account granted to the app. It has to be connected again, with a fresh sign-in, to be used.

404.description: No connected app with that id

post.summary: Sign out (end the key this request used)
post.description: Deletes the API key sent with this request, so it stops working everywhere; the account's other keys and connected apps are untouched. The dashboard's Sign out calls this before it clears the key from the browser. Needs one of the account's own keys (the admin env key or a connected app gets 400 not_an_account_key).

204.description: Signed out; the key no longer works

400.description: Not one of the account's own keys (code not_an_account_key)

get.summary: List your API keys
get.description: Every key on the account, newest first. `current` marks the key this request was made with. Keys issued before names existed have no `name` or `last4` (shown as "Earlier key"). `last_used_at` is updated at most every 5 minutes. A key unused for 180 days stops working. `idle_expires_at` says when (KEY_IDLE_EXPIRY_DAYS); one minted with `expires_in_days` stops at `expires_at`. A key that has stopped stays listed with `expired` until revoked.

post.summary: Create a named API key
post.description: Mints a new key with the given name (for a CI secret or another machine) and returns it once; it is stored only as a hash. `scope: deploy` makes a deploy-only key: it may create, update, roll back and list sites, read their versions and files, and make preview links; every other route (delete, rename, domains, keys, saved data and lists, analytics, the account, AI create, connecting apps, and the same through /mcp) answers 403 deploy_only_key. Use it for a CI secret. `expires_in_days` (1-3650) gives the key a fixed expiry; without it the key stops only when it goes unused (KEY_IDLE_EXPIRY_DAYS). Needs one of the account's own keys (the admin env key or a connected app gets 400 not_an_account_key). An account holds at most 50 keys (409 key_limit; keys that have stopped working do not count, and are deleted 30 days after they stop). A deploy key never carries admin powers. A deploy key can publish code that runs when you open your own site (signed in there, that code acts with your powers over its saved data); treat it like the site itself; a key revoked or rotated away mid-request gets 401 invalid_api_key.

name.description: Any label except the names Simple Host gives its own keys (dashboard sign-in, agent sign-in, event account, reviewer sign-in, replacement key; 400)

scope.description: deploy: create, update, roll back and list sites and make preview links, nothing else

expires_in_days.description: Optional fixed expiry, in days from now

201.description: Key created. `api_key` is shown only here.

409.description: The account already holds 50 keys (code key_limit); revoke one first.

delete.summary: Revoke one API key
delete.description: The key stops working at once; the account's other keys and connected apps are untouched. Revoking the key this request uses signs this caller out. Needs one of the account's own keys.

400.description: Not one of the account's own keys (code not_an_account_key)

404.description: No key with that id on this account

get.summary: List your sites
get.description: Returns the authenticated user's sites. Admins see all sites.

post.summary: Deploy a site from inline JSON files
post.description: The LLM-friendly deploy path — send every file inline in one request, no archiving. Text goes in `files`; base64-encoded binary goes in `files_base64`. `index.html` is required. Relative paths only (`..`/absolute are rejected); secret files (`.env`, `.git/*`, `id_rsa`) are dropped and script extensions (`.sh .py .php …`) are rejected. Use PUT to update an existing site (409 site_exists says so); PUT with ?create=1 creates or updates in one call.

put.summary: Update a site from inline JSON files
put.description: Same as POST, but for an existing site you own. Creates a new version and activates it; with ?publish=false the version is only stored (visitors keep seeing the live one) and the answer adds unpublished_version, preview_url and preview_expires_at. With ?create=1 a missing site is created instead (201, with the same checks as POST), so CI deploys in one call; without it a missing site is 404.

201.description: Site created (?create=1 and no site of that name)

patch.summary: Rename your site, or take it offline
patch.description: One change per request. With {"offline": true} the site is taken offline: every address answers a plain "This site is offline" page (503), and visitor saves (state and collection writes from a page, private lists included), visitors' reads of its state and lists, and visitor sign-in are refused with 403 site_offline; files, versions and saved data are kept, and the owner's key or connector still deploys, reads and writes. {"offline": false} puts it back online. An operator take-down wins over it, and a taken-down site cannot be switched (403 site_suspended). The answer is the site object with `offline` and a `note`. With {"name": "new-name"} it renames the database row and on-disk site directory. The new name uses the same validation and per-owner uniqueness rule as creation. A bound custom domain remains attached. Links to the old name keep working: its site host, person-path and sites.* addresses 302 to the new address (path and query kept), through any chain of renames, until a site with the old name is created again (the new site wins); the response says so with old_url_status "redirects". Deleting the site stops the redirects (restoring brings them back); purging it removes them.

schema.description: Exactly one of name or offline.

offline.description: true takes the site offline; false puts it back online.

200.description: Renamed (old_name, name, old_url, site_url, old_url_status) or switched (the site object with offline and note)

403.description: The operator has taken the site down (code site_suspended)

post.summary: Create a site from an archive
post.description: Upload a `.tar.gz` or `.zip` (for framework builds, binary assets, large sites). Max 100 MB.

put.summary: Update a site from an archive
put.description: Upload a new version of an existing site you own. Creates a new version and activates it; with ?publish=false the version is only stored (visitors keep seeing the live one) and the answer adds unpublished_version, preview_url and preview_expires_at. With ?create=1 a missing site is created instead (201, with the same checks as POST): one call from CI, e.g. `curl -X PUT ".../v1/sites/<name>?create=1" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" --data-binary @site.tar.gz`.

201.description: Site created (?create=1 and no site of that name)

delete.summary: Delete your site
delete.description: Takes the site offline at once, with every version, its saved state and collections. It stays in Recently deleted (GET /v1/me/deleted-sites) for 7 days with its name held, and POST /v1/sites/{sitename}/restore brings it back exactly as it was; after that it is removed for good. Creating a site with a held name answers 409 with recently_deleted true.

post.summary: Restore a recently deleted site
post.description: Brings a site back from Recently deleted under the same name and address, with every version, its saved data, collections and connected address, live at once.

404.description: No site with that name in Recently deleted

409.description: That site is live

get.summary: Download a site as a tar.gz
get.description: Streams the site's published files (`files/`), its saved JSON state (`state.json`) and its collections (`collections.json`: every list, private ones included, each entry as `{id, created_at, submitted_by, data}`; `submitted_by` only on private lists) as one archive. Exists because an event instance is destroyed when the event ends and nothing is backed up, so the person who built something can take it with them. The saved data comes first: the files usually exist somewhere else, the JSON only lives here.

404.description: Not found

post.summary: Make a 10-minute download link for a site's export
post.description: Returns a link that downloads the same archive as `export.tar.gz` without an API key, for people who use Simple Host only through a chat app's connector (the `export_site` tool). The link is signed for this owner and this site, expires after 10 minutes, and stops working if the site is deleted or the server restarts. Anyone holding it can download the copy until then, so hand it to the person only.

get.summary: Download a site's export through a link from export-link

get.summary: Get per-site visitor analytics

Owner-scoped view and visitor counts derived server-side from the access log (no client beacon). Every bucket is split three ways by who was asking: `person` (no automation signature), `bot` (crawlers, AI scrapers, SEO tools, security scanners, HTTP libraries) and `infra` (uptime probes and health checks aimed at the site). Read `person` as the audience number — a total that folds in `infra` is dominated by monitoring, not people.

`visitors` are unique visitors: COUNT(DISTINCT hashed IP) over the window asked for. The salt is stable, so `totals.*.visitors` is genuine uniques for the range and is NOT the sum of the `daily` figures — someone who visited on five days is one unique in `totals` and five in `daily`. IP-based, so a shared office NAT reads as one visitor and a phone switching wifi→cellular reads as two.

`daily` is zero-filled dense for the requested window (oldest → newest). `hourly` is always 24 zero-filled buckets ending with the hour in progress. Only successful document responses (200/304, non-asset paths) count as views, for every class alike. Owner only (API key).

`country` is ISO-3166 alpha-2. `"XX"` / `"Unknown"` is traffic the table could not place (an unlisted block, or a server whose ranges have not been loaded); it is listed rather than dropped, so the countries still add up to the site's totals.

Someone whose address changes country mid-range counts once in each, so the columns can total slightly more than the site's own figure. `unknown` is always zero here: the pre-classifier history has no addresses left to place. The email setting is the owner's and is not shown.

put.summary: Declare what a data name is (owner)
put.description: Owner only (X-API-Key, connector token, or the operator). Every piece of saved data has a name and one kind, and the kind decides who reads and who changes what. `{"kind": "content"}` is **Page info**: one JSON object only the owner writes (PUT .../data/{coll}) and anyone reads; a site declares at most 20 Page info names (SAVED_DATA_CONTENT_NAMES_MAX, 409 too_many_names); a name holding several entries cannot become one (409 has_entries). `{"kind": "entries"}` is **Submissions**: things visitors send. Options: `visibility` (`owner`, the default: only the owner reads them all, each visitor reads their own; or `public`: anyone reads them, without who sent them), `one_per_person` (one live entry per signed-in visitor), `notify` (email the owner: `daily`, the default while private; `each`, batched soon after they arrive; `off`, the default when public). A field left out keeps what the name had. A name nobody declared is **Shared** (anyone reads it, anyone signed in adds to it); with SAVED_DATA_DEFAULT_KIND=declare_first, on a site made after the kinds it takes no saves at all (409 declare_first). Product words are accepted for kind ("Page info", "Submissions"). Submissions need the site on an address of its own, where visitors sign in (409 custom_domain_required on instances without one); a site declares at most 50 Submissions names (SAVED_DATA_ENTRIES_NAMES_MAX, 409 too_many_names). Declaring a private name that holds entries as public Submissions would let anyone read them: 409 confirm_public (with `count`) until the request carries `"confirm_public": true`. A private name becomes Page info only while it is empty (409 has_entries). Both count what is in the name's Recently deleted too (a restore brings it back) and are checked under the name's lock. Public Submissions are refused on an install with WRITE_AUTH_MODE=off (409 visitor_sign_in_off). `{"kind": "mine"}` is **Personal**: one private record per signed-in visitor (a habit tracker, saved progress), stored private. Simple Host's owner tools (key, connector, owner app, exports) never show a person's record: the owner sees how many people have one and their size (from 3 people up). The site's own pages run in the visitor's browser and can read that visitor's record, so Personal is as private as the site's pages are trustworthy. A name holds records for at most 1,000 people (SAVED_DATA_PERSONAL_PEOPLE_MAX; a new person past it: 409 people_full). A name must be empty (nothing live or in Recently deleted) to become Personal (409 has_entries), and a Personal name that holds records never becomes another kind (409 has_records; both checked under the name's lock, so no save lands in between); a site declares at most 20 Personal names (SAVED_DATA_PERSONAL_NAMES_MAX). `{"kind": "board"}` is a **Shared board**: anyone reads it; signed-in visitors add, change and delete items one at a time; only the owner clears it; private entries become a board only with `confirm_public`; a site declares at most 20 Shared board names (SAVED_DATA_BOARD_NAMES_MAX). Neither takes options (400 invalid_kind), and both need the site's own address (409 custom_domain_required). Product words are accepted ("Personal", "Shared board").

get.description: Page info (`content`) answers `{name, kind, data, saved_at}` (`data` null until the owner saves one) to anyone. A Shared board (`board`) answers as a public list, each item with its `version`, plus an `ETag` (304 while unchanged: poll with `If-None-Match`). Submissions answer exactly as GET .../collections/{coll} does (the owner reads all, with `by`; anyone reads a public list, without who sent it; a private list is 404 not_found to everyone else), with `?count=1` for `{name, count}` under the same rule, and `?mine=1` for the signed-in visitor's own live entries (a visitor session on the site's own address; `?limit`, `?before` as for lists; 401 visitor_auth_required without one). An undeclared name is Shared and reads as a list; where the install requires declaring first: 409 declare_first.

post.summary: Add a Submissions entry
post.description: The same as POST .../collections/{coll} (same sign-in, Origin, privacy, `Idempotency-Key` and per-address rules), with the name's kind applied: Each new entry is at most 16 KB (SAVED_DATA_ENTRY_MAX_KB, 413 item_too_large); a name holds at most 10,000 live entries (SAVED_DATA_ENTRIES_MAX, 409 list_full); `one_per_person` refuses a second live entry from one visitor (409 one_per_person, with `id` of the entry they have; a visitor is the account, and its address with any +tag, so an entry from another account of the same address answers without `id`). Declared Submissions take entries only from a signed-in visitor (401 visitor_auth_required), never anonymously. Page info takes no entries (409 wrong_kind). An undeclared name is Shared and takes what the list route takes; where the install requires declaring first, nothing (409 declare_first). The site's who-may-save setting applies to every visitor (403 not_allowed_to_save; a block also matches the address with its +tag dropped); the owner always may. A Shared board takes one JSON object per item from a signed-in visitor on the site's own address (or the owner's key): each item is at most 16 KB (SAVED_DATA_BOARD_ITEM_MAX_KB) and a board holds at most 2,000 live items (SAVED_DATA_BOARD_MAX, 409 list_full); `_submitted_by` and `_submitted_at` are dropped from what is sent (the server's own stamps); board adds, changes and deletes are limited per address and, whatever the address, to 30 a minute per signed-in person (SAVED_DATA_BOARD_WRITES_PER_MIN; 429 rate_limited); the answer carries the item's `version` (1). A Personal name takes no items (409 wrong_kind): its visitor writes their record with PUT or PATCH.

409.description: declare_first, wrong_kind, one_per_person, list_full or kind_changed (the owner changed what the name is, or made it private or public, while the save was on its way; nothing was saved)

put.description: Replaces a Page info document with one JSON object. A Page info document is at most 1 MB (SAVED_DATA_CONTENT_MAX_KB; 413 item_too_large); not an object: 400 not_an_object. Only the owner: their X-API-Key or connector token (no page Origin needed), the operator, or the owner signed in on the site's own address with `X-SH-CSRF: 1`. Anyone else: 403 owner_only (another account's key: 404). The earlier document goes to the name's history (GET .../collections/{coll}/history; restore with .../history/{id}/restore). Submissions and Shared boards: 409 wrong_kind; undeclared: 409 declare_first. On a Personal name this is the signed-in visitor replacing their own record with one JSON object (a visitor session on the site's own address, `X-SH-CSRF: 1`, who may save here; the per-address write rate applies; `Idempotency-Key` honoured); A personal record is at most 64 KB (SAVED_DATA_PERSONAL_MAX_KB; 413 item_too_large). A visitor with no record yet is refused once the name holds records for 1,000 people (SAVED_DATA_PERSONAL_PEOPLE_MAX; 409 people_full). The answer is `{name, kind, data, version}`. A key never writes anyone's record (403 personal_data).

put.summary: Make a collection private or public
put.description: Owner only (X-API-Key, or a connector token as `Authorization: Bearer`). `{"private": true}` makes the list private: only visitors signed in on the site's own address can add to it (each item stamped with their verified email), and only the owner can read it (key, connector, CSV export, dashboard, or the owner signed in on the site) — plus the Simple Host operator, for moderation. Everyone else gets 404. The owner can edit or delete its items (PATCH/DELETE .../items/{id}); in a public list the owner can delete items but not edit them (409 append_only). Any site can make a list private. Submissions come from signed-in visitors on the site's own address: its address `https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.site/`, or its domain if it has one. Can be set before any item exists. `{"private": false}` makes it public again, and everything already in it becomes readable by anyone, except who sent it: `_submitted_by` is left out of every read but the owner's (key, or signed in on the site's own address) and the admin's. While the list holds entries that is 409 confirm_public (with `count`) until the request carries `"confirm_public": true`, after the owner agreed. On declared Submissions it is 409 visitor_sign_in_off on an install with WRITE_AUTH_MODE=off. Idempotent; deletes nothing.

get.summary: Changes to a site's saved data (owner)
get.description: Every change to the site's saved-data document in the last 30 days (SAVED_DATA_UNDO_DAYS), newest first, without the values: what happened (`op`: replace for a PUT, change for a PATCH, restore), who made it (`by`, the address they were signed in with; `by_kind` owner, admin, visitor or anonymous; the operator's moderation shows as "Simple Host (operator)") and when. post.summary: Give this site a nicer address (free <name>.simple-host.site or a custom domain)
post.description:
Optional. Every site already lives at its own address `https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.site/`, with sign-in and private lists. This gives it a nicer address; the site moves there and its old address redirects. A free address: send `{"domain": "<name>.simple-host.site"}` (one DNS label: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not at the start or end, up to 63 characters). It is active at once with no DNS step — the answer has `status: active` and `verified_at`, and no `dns`. First come, first served: 409 domain_taken if another site holds it or it is already someone's handle (handles and free names share one namespace); reserved names (www, sites, api, admin, mail, cname and the platform's own hosts) get 400 name_reserved; anything else malformed gets 400 invalid_name. Once claimed it behaves exactly like a custom domain: the site is served at its root with a same-origin /v1 API and visitor sign-in, its person-address URL 302s there, and private collections take submissions there. A site has one own address: claiming one replaces a custom domain and vice versa. A free name the site lets go (switching, DELETE, or deleting the site) stays with it: it redirects to the site's current address and nobody else can claim it. A custom domain: bind ONE domain to the site (status starts as `pending`). Returns the two DNS records the owner must create: `dns` (CNAME for a subdomain, A for an apex) and `dns_txt`, the ownership record (TXT `_simple-host.<domain>` holding this site's token), which proves the domain is theirs and must stay in place. Nothing is verified or certified without it. A name another site on this server already serves is refused by the certificate issuer (failed, "already served here"). Once both records are seen, its certificate is requested automatically (at most 5 new domain certificates per account per day) (`certificate_status`: pending → issuing → live, or failed with the reason in `last_error`, retried) and the domain is served at its root, usually within minutes. If the site already has a working own address (a free name or an earlier domain), it keeps serving there (`previous_domain`) until the new domain is verified; then the old address redirects to it. Binding the site's current working domain again changes nothing; binding its `previous_domain` drops the pending one. Until first verified, a binding is provisional: another site can take it over until it has passed its ownership proof, and it expires 24 hours after binding unless DNS already points here. A verified domain stays exclusive while it works; if it fails every check for 24 hours the owner is emailed, and after 72 hours it is disconnected (the site's own address serves again) and can be connected afresh, with the TXT record, by whoever holds it; while it is being released, binding it answers 409 domain_releasing. Hijacking the platform zone is rejected. Owner only (API key).

www and the bare domain (where the certificate issuer runs, as on simple-host.app; absent elsewhere): binding `example.com` also sets up `www.example.com` (and binding `www.example.com` sets up `example.com`) as a redirect-only host that forwards (301) to the name chosen. The answer names it (`partner_domain`) with the record it needs (`dns_partner`); the TXT record on the chosen name covers both. It goes on the same certificate only if it points here and no other site on this server answers it; otherwise the chosen name goes live alone and `partner_status` is `not_set_up` with `partner_note` saying why.

post.summary: Ask one of the "Ask" assistants on the public pages
post.description: Powers the two "Ask" assistants: Simple Host (on the features and architecture pages) and Simple Host Enterprise (on the three enterprise pages). Answers in one to three short sentences (more, up to about 150 words, when the reader asks for detail or steps), only from the assistant's text built into the server: a short public summary plus the visible text of all its pages (for the architecture page a curated summary). The page the reader is on is preferred, and an answer may link to the assistant's other pages. The older form, page alone without assistant, still works for one release and picks that page's assistant. Runs on the same single model backend as AI create (xAI's Grok), with no fallback. Only the question and that text are sent to the model — nothing about the visitor. The question text is never stored or logged; standard web server logs apply. No sign-in. Send Accept: text/event-stream to get the answer as it is written (the page's widget does); without it the answer comes back in one JSON object. The first words must arrive within 20 seconds and the whole answer within 45. Absent when the server has no model backend configured or ASK_ENABLED is off.

post.summary: Check the setup helper's changed settings for likely mistakes
post.description: Powers the optional "Check my choices" step of the setup helper at /setup, just before it shows the files. Send the product and the settings changed from their defaults, names and values only. Only settings of that product's list (the setup helper's settings files) whose type is a number, duration, switch, choice or rate are accepted: a secret is refused (secret_not_accepted) and so is free text such as a hostname or email (setting_not_checkable), and every value must be one the setting allows. The model (the same backend, ASK_MODEL and ASK_REASONING_EFFORT as the Ask assistants) sees those settings, each with its default, plus the settings list and known interactions between settings; nothing about the visitor is sent. Every finding is checked against the settings list before it is returned: one naming an unknown, secret or free-text setting, or suggesting a value outside a setting's allowed range, is dropped. A finding whose suggestion would make a security-sensitive setting looser than both its default and the value sent (a longer lifetime, a looser rate, an insecure switch on, a less strict choice) keeps its message without the suggestion. Values are printable ASCII; suggested rates come back as <burst><separator><interval> with no spaces, numbers without leading zeros; messages carry no links. The settings are never stored or logged. No sign-in. Same-origin only, as /v1/ask: no CORS grant, an application/json body, and the Origin must be this server's own address. Shares the Ask per-IP and per-network rate limits; its own limit on checks at once (SETUP_CHECK_MAX_IN_FLIGHT, default 1), a cap per network (/24 or /48) per UTC day (SETUP_CHECK_PER_NETWORK_DAILY, default 20) and a cap per UTC day across everyone (SETUP_CHECK_DAILY_MAX, default 200; 0 turns it off). Send the product, where the visitor is in the form, their choices (exactly what /v1/setup/check accepts: settings of that product's list whose type is a number, duration, switch, choice or rate, with an allowed value; a secret is refused with secret_not_accepted, free text with setting_not_checkable), the basic answers picked from fixed lists (small-box: codes, google; enterprise: idp, certs, smtp, bucket, creds), the message, optionally pasted error output, and the last few turns. get.description: Streams every site on the instance as one .tar.gz, each under `<handle>/<site>/` in the same layout as GET /v1/sites/{sitename}/export.tar.gz: `state.json` (saved data), `collections.json` (every list, private ones included) and `files/` (the live version). For an organiser keeping every entry before the box is deleted. Non-admin callers receive 404.

connector.description: Per-person OAuth 2.1 (authorization code; PKCE S256 required for every self-registered client). An access token sent as `Authorization: Bearer` acts exactly as that person's X-API-Key on every route here. Discovery at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.

scopes.sites: Publish and manage your sites and their data

path.name: path
path.description: Relative file path (may contain forward slashes)

create.name: create
create.description: 1 creates the site when you have none of that name (reserved names, the site quota and publish=false are refused as on POST), so one PUT deploys from CI whether or not the site exists

publish.name: publish
publish.description: false stores the new version without making it live (updates only; a new site's first version always goes live: 400)

idempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
idempotencyKey.description: Any unique string per write (e.g. a random UUID). For a writer with an identity (the owner's key or connector, or a visitor signed in on the site) a retry with the same key and the same body on the same site and route is saved once, for 24 hours (SAVED_DATA_IDEMPOTENCY_HOURS), and answered with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`: an append with the item it made, a PATCH with the document as it is now and its ETag. The same key with a different body gets 409 idempotency_key_reused; while the first request is still running, 409 idempotency_in_progress; a failed request is not remembered. Writes made without signing in ignore the header. Longer than 255 characters: 400 invalid_idempotency_key.

Savers.description: Who may save on a site.

mode.description: anyone: anyone who signs in; listed: only allow (the owner always may)

allow.description: Emails and @domains who may save when mode is listed

block.description: Emails and @domains who may never save

visitors.description: Unique visitors — distinct hashed IPs over this bucket's window

TrafficSplit.description: One bucket of traffic, split by who was asking. `person` is the audience figure; `infra` is the site's own monitoring and is normally far larger than either of the other two. `unknown` is non-zero only for days before `classified_from`, which were recorded before traffic was classified and cannot be broken down after the fact — do not fold it into any of the other three.

name.description: Where it came from (dashboard sign-in, agent sign-in, event account, replacement key) or the name typed when it was created. Absent on keys issued before names existed.

scope.description: full, or deploy (create, update, roll back and list sites and make preview links only)

expires_at.description: The fixed expiry chosen when it was minted; null for none

idle_expires_at.description: When it stops working unless used before then; null when idle expiry is off

expired.description: Present once the key has stopped working: past expires_at (expired) or unused too long (idle)

current.description: This is the key the request was made with

api_key.description: A new key for this sign-in, starting shk_ (keys issued before 2026-09-27 are bare hex and keep working). Earlier keys keep working until revoked (DELETE /v1/me/keys/{id}) or rotated. Stored only as a hash, so it is shown only here.

created.description: true if this verify created the account

files_base64.description: relative path -> base64-encoded binary contents. A path cannot also appear in `files`.

site_url.description: The link to share: https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.site/ (briefly https://<handle>.simple-host.site/<site>/ for a brand-new account), or the site's domain when it has one

custom_domain.description: The site's free <name>.simple-host.site address or its own domain, when it has one

deployed_at.description: When the newest version went live (site list only)

domain_last_error.description: Site list only, for a domain that is not active: what the last check found

domain_expires_at.description: Site list only: when an unproven domain binding is released (24 h after binding; absent once DNS points here)

domain_certificate_status.description: Site list only, for a domain not live yet: its certificate

previous_domain.description: Site list only, for a domain not live yet: the earlier address the site keeps answering at until it is

domain_dns.description: Site list only, for an own domain that is not active: the DNS record that points it here, to add at the registrar

domain_dns_txt.description: Site list only, for an own domain that is not active: the TXT ownership record to add next to domain_dns (_simple-host.<domain> holding the site's token)

suspended.description: Present and true when the operator has taken the site down (on its own or with its owner's account): every address shows a "taken down" page and changes are refused until it is restored. Nothing is deleted.

offline.description: Present and true when the owner has taken the site offline (PATCH /v1/sites/{sitename} {"offline": true}): every address shows "This site is offline" and visitor saves are refused. Nothing is deleted.

unpublished_version.description: Only on a deploy with publish=false: the version stored without going live.

preview_url.description: Only on a deploy with publish=false: a link showing the stored version that works for anyone with it, for one hour.

domain_partner.description: The custom domain's www / bare partner, which forwards to it (see GET .../domain partner_domain)

domain_partner_dns.description: The record that points the partner here too

domain_partner_note.description: Why the partner is not set up, when it is not

keep.description: Site list only: the owner marked the site Keep; it is never flagged as idle (PUT .../keep)

idle_removal_at.description: Site list only: the site had no visits by people and no new version for 90 days and its owner was emailed; it moves to Recently deleted at this time unless it is kept, visited or updated

AddressState.description: The account's own site address (https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.site/) and its certificate. On GET /v1/me always (on simple-host.app, once the account has a handle); on a site (address_state) only while that site is still at its interim address https://<handle>.simple-host.site/<site>/. When the address switches, old links redirect, but visitors' sign-ins and what their browser kept for the site start fresh.

state.description: ready; waiting (the certificate is queued behind the weekly and daily limits); failing (it could not be issued yet and is retried automatically)

address.description: The own address: on /v1/me the pattern https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.site/, on a site that site's address

interim_address.description: Where sites are until then (waiting or failing)

ready_in_hours.description: The same, in whole hours, at least 1

note.description: A plain sentence to show the person (waiting or failing)

last_activity.description: Latest of: created, last deploy, last visit by a person, last Keep

suspended_by.description: Which switch holds it down: its own, or its owner's account

code.description: A stable snake_case name for the refusal, present where one status has more than one meaning. site_exists (409: this account already has a site of that name), domain_taken (409: the address belongs to another site or person), invalid_name (400: not 1-63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens), name_reserved (400: reserved by the platform), invalid_domain (400: not a domain that can be connected), site_quota_reached (403), append_only (409: public list items cannot be edited; the owner may still delete them), custom_domain_required (409: the site needs its own address first), not_an_object (409: the saved value is not a JSON object), private_visitor_only and private_needs_own_domain (403), use_custom_domain and visitor_auth_required (401), missing_api_key, wrong_auth_header (sent Authorization instead of X-API-Key), invalid_api_key (unknown, revoked or signed-out key), key_expired (past the expiry chosen when it was minted) and key_expired_idle (unused too long, KEY_IDLE_EXPIRY_DAYS) (401), deploy_only_key (403: a deploy-only key on a route it may not call), csrf_required (403), recently_deleted (409: the name belongs to a site in Recently deleted), site_not_deleted (409: restore of a live site), confirm_required (400), not_found (404, private collections), export_link_invalid (404: the download link expired or is not valid), site_suspended (403: the operator has taken the site down; changes and public reads of its data are refused until it is restored, `reason` says why), account_suspended (403: the operator has suspended this account; its keys, connected apps and sign-in are refused, `reason` says why), site_offline (403: the owner has taken the site offline; visitor saves are refused until it is back online, the owner's key still writes), preview_read_only (403: a save made from a page opened as a version preview), preview_unavailable (409: the site has no address of its own to preview on), invalid_request (400). New codes may be added.

BadRequest.description: Invalid request. A saved-data write whose JSON holds a NUL character (\u0000), half of a surrogate pair or bytes that are not UTF-8 is code invalid_json.

Unauthorized.description: Missing or invalid API key — send the X-API-Key header, not Authorization Bearer. The body's code is missing_api_key, wrong_auth_header, invalid_api_key, key_expired or key_expired_idle (create a new key from the Keys panel).

Conflict.description: Conflict: the code says which (site_exists, domain_taken, append_only, custom_domain_required, not_an_object)

TooLarge.description: Payload too large (on saved data, code item_too_large)

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limited (code rate_limited). Saved-data reads allow 30 a second per address with a burst of 60 (SAVED_DATA_READ_PER_SEC, SAVED_DATA_READ_BURST).

SiteFull.description: The write would grow the site's live saved data (the page-data document plus live list items; history and Recently deleted are not counted) past 50 MB (SAVED_DATA_SITE_MAX_MB) (code site_full). Writes that do not grow it always go through; deleting list items or clearing a list makes room at once.

example.error: this site's saved data is full (50 MB of page data and list items); the owner can delete list items or clear lists to make room

OriginMismatch.description: Origin/Referer is not one of the site's own addresses (code origin_not_allowed). An agent or script sends the site owner's X-API-Key and no Origin or Referer, which needs no page.
